title: Vrabel-led anti-government rally and march in Prague
location: Wenceslas Square, then a march through central Prague to Strakova Academy (Office of Government)
scope: Prague gathering and march; no broader geographic scope established
organizer: Ladislav Vrabel and ČR na 1. místě
participants_original: A Prague police spokesperson said several hundred people attended; organizer Ladislav Vrabel claimed thousands. The source does not give an exact count.
threshold_50_evidence: The police spokesperson's qualitative estimate of several hundred participants clearly exceeds 50; no exact numerical bound is supplied.

start_date.summary: Contemporaneous reports date the gathering to Saturday, 21 January 2023; iROZHLAS says it began at 13:00. Drbna describes the same start time in coverage published while the event was still under way.

end_date.summary: iROZHLAS reports that after speeches and the march to the Office of Government, Vrabel ended the demonstration after 16:30 on 21 January; publication timing and later reporting do not extend the physical episode beyond that date.

location.summary: The gathering began on Wenceslas Square and the executed march went through central Prague to Strakova Academy, the Office of Government.

scope.summary: One organized Prague square gathering and associated march are described; no broader geographic event scope is established.

organizer.summary: Reports identify Ladislav Vrabel and the ČR na 1. místě association as organizers.

demands.summary: Reports document calls for the government to resign and criticism of government policy, including support for Ukraine and NATO, alongside criticism of presidential candidate Petr Pavel. The event was not solely a candidate-support rally.

participants_original.summary: Reports describe several hundred participants; S001 and S002 attribute that qualitative estimate to a Prague police spokesperson, while S001 also reports Vrabel claimed thousands. The repeated police estimate is not independent corroboration; no exact count or numeric bounds are supported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Both reports describe a police estimate of several hundred participants, which clearly exceeds the 50-person threshold; the wording is qualitative and does not justify numeric bounds.

protester_violence.summary: Unknown. S001 reports two young people threw paint at Vrabel and others but does not establish their affiliation or whether they were event participants.

state_response.summary: Unknown. S001 mentions police presence. S002 reports a person was detained during the gathering over suspected online conduct from November, but does not connect the detention to the protest; no state-response category can be attributed to the event from these reports.

notes: The event occurred during the presidential election period and speakers criticized candidate Petr Pavel, but contemporary reporting also documents direct anti-government demands, including calls for the government to resign and criticism of its policies. It is therefore not described solely as electoral support. The square gathering and its same-day march are treated as one organized physical episode; end time is after 16:30 on 21 January. S001 credits ČTK; S002 is a separately bylined iDNES newsroom report. S001 and S002 report a similar police crowd estimate, so it is not independent numerical corroboration. Drbna carries a named byline and says the outlet uses ČTK material generally, but the story-specific relationship is unknown. A person detained during the event was suspected of November online conduct, not conduct at the event. The paint throwers’ affiliation is unknown.
open_questions: Seek a genuinely independent contemporaneous crowd estimate; preserve qualitative wording unless a source provides a defensible count.
Check whether any official police statement connects the reported detention to this protest; current reporting does not.
Clarify the affiliation of the people who threw paint and any official response if supported by contemporaneous evidence.
Coordinator should reassess the Jan 8 candidate-support gathering if evidence establishes that participants made a distinct state-directed assembly or policy demand.
